cues.text: Hello. Children's Engineering Workshops.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: Oh hello. I wanted some information about the workshops in the school holidays.
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Sure.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: I have two daughters who are interested. The younger one's Lydia, she's four - do you take children as young as that?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Yes, our Tiny Engineers workshop is for four to five-year-olds.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: What sorts of activities do they do?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: All sorts. For example, they work together to design a special cover that goes round an egg, so that when it's inside they can drop it from a height and it doesn't break. Well, sometimes it does break but that's part of the fun!
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: Right. And Lydia loves building things. Is there any opportunity for her to do that?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Well, they have a competition to see who can make the highest tower. You'd be amazed how high they can go.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: Right
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: But they're learning all the time as well as having fun. For example, one thing they do is to design and build a car that's attached to a balloon, and the force of the air in that actually powers the car and makes it move along. They go really fast too.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: OK, well, all this sounds perfect.
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Now Carly, that's my older daughter, has just had her seventh birthday, so presumably she'd be in a different group?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Yes, she'd be in the Junior Engineers. That's for children from six to eight.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: And do they do the same sorts of activities?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Some are the same, but a bit more advanced. So they work out how to build model vehicles, things like cars and trucks, but also how to construct animals using the same sorts of material and technique, and then they learn how they can program them and make them move.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: So they learn a bit of coding?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: They do. They pick it up really quickly. We're there to help if they need it, but they learn from one another too.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: Right. And do they have competitions too?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Yes, with the Junior Engineers, it's to use recycled materials like card and wood to build a bridge, and the longest one gets a prize.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: That sounds fun. I wouldn't mind doing that myself!
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Then they have something a bit different, which is to think up an idea for a five-minute movie and then film it, using special animation software. You'd be amazed what they come up with.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: And of course, that's something they can put on their phone and take home to show all their friends.
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Exactly. And then they also build a robot in the shape of a human, and they decorate it and program it so that it can move its arms and legs.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: Perfect. So, is it the same price as the Tiny Engineers?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: It's just a bit more: £50 for the five weeks.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: And are the classes on a Monday, too?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: They used to be, but we found it didn't give our staff enough time to clear up after the first workshop, so we moved them to Wednesdays. The classes are held in the morning from ten to eleven.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: OK. That's better for me actually. And what about the location? Where exactly are the workshops held?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: They're in building 10A - there's a big sign on the door, you can't miss it, and that's in Fradstone Industrial Estate.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: Sorry?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Fradstone - that's F-R-A-D-S-T-O-N-E.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: And that's in Grasford, isn't it?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: Yes, up past the station.
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: And will I have any parking problems there?
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: No, there's always plenty available. So would you like to enrol Lydia and Carly now?
cues.speaker: SARAH

cues.text: ОК.
cues.speaker: FATHER

cues.text: So can I have your full name ...
cues.speaker: SARAH
